TECHNOVA 
Exit and Resignation Procedure2026 
Effective Date: June 15, 2026 
Version: 1.0 
Approved By: Human Resources Operations and Central IT Security Infrastructure Teams. 
1.0 Resignation and Notification Procedures 
1.1 Separation Guidelines 
A structured, transparent exit procedure ensures operational continuity, smooth task handovers, and 
a positive long-term relationship between Technova and departing team members. This policy is 
designed to make the offboarding track simple and clear for both employees and management. 
1.2 Submission of Voluntary Resignation 
When an employee chooses to leave their role at Technova, the separation workflow formally begins 
with a written notification. 
• 
Formal Notice Requirement: As highlighted in our core guidelines, employees must provide 
a minimum of two (2) weeks' written notice to their direct manager and the HR Operations 
team. 
• 
HRIS Logging: In addition to notifying the manager, the employee must formally log their 
resignation date and last working day requests within the self-service HRIS portal to initiate 
the offboarding track. 
• 
Notice Period Dynamics: Elective paid time off (PTO) is generally not permitted during the 
active notice period to ensure proper handover execution, except in verified medical 
emergencies. 
1.3 Involuntary Separation Protocols 
In instances involving business restructuring or performance-based terminations, the separation 
process is managed directly by departmental leadership in tight coordination with HR. Official 
notification, final day parameters, and severance logic are delivered in writing, ensuring strict 
compliance with local labor frameworks. 
2.0 Knowledge Transfer and Handover Checkpoints 
2.1 Protecting Engineering and Operational Continuity 
To prevent project delays, departing team members must comprehensively document and transition 
their active responsibilities before their final day of active service. 
2.2 Constructing the Handover Document 
During their final two weeks, the departing employee must compile a clear handover brief within 
their team's shared documentation space. This brief must cover: 
• 
A complete inventory of active projects, software development tracks, and immediate 
delivery deadlines.

• 
Direct status updates on outstanding issues, client requests, and core cross-department 
dependencies. 
• 
Clear links to relevant code repositories, system technical designs, and engineering 
runbooks. 
2.3 Task Assignment and Peer Synchronization 
Managers will review the handover brief and immediately reassign active ownership parameters to 
remaining team members. Dedicated walkthrough sessions must be scheduled during the final week 
so the departing employee can sync directly with the peer taking over their daily responsibilities. 
3.0 Technical Asset Reclamation and Access Revocation 
3.1 Revoking Digital Identity and Infrastructure Access 
Securing Technova’s proprietary codebases, client environments, and internal networks requires 
systematic de-provisioning of data access permissions. 
3.2 Automated Account Termination 
At 5:30 PM on the employee's confirmed final working day, automated IT scripts execute profile 
deactivation. 
• 
Corporate Directory Deactivation: Central IT disables access to corporate email, messaging 
channels, and internal HRIS dashboards. 
• 
Engineering Environment Revocation: Permissions are stripped from secure cloud 
environments, API consoles, deployment tools, and repository networks. 
• 
Single Sign-On (SSO) Shutdown: Core corporate login keys are fully revoked, blocking all 
inbound connection paths to company tools. 
3.3 Return of Company-Issued Hardware 
All physical assets belonging to Technova must be returned in good working condition. Local 
employees must hand over their devices to the office IT helpdesk on their final day, while remote 
staff will receive a pre-paid shipping container to return their equipment within 48 hours of 
separation. Returned items include: 
• 
Company-issued laptops, power adapters, and diagnostic testing accessories. 
• 
Corporate mobile phones, secondary authentication keys, and specialized technical hardware 
components. 
• 
Physical facility security badges, office keys, and parking access passes. 
4.0 Final Settlement, Clearances, and Exit Interviews 
4.1 Administrative Closure and Financial Settlement 
Finalizing your employment history at Technova involves clearing outstanding expense reports and 
processing your final paycheck smoothly. 
4.2 Expense Reports and Final Payout Processing

• 
Expense Submissions: All business travel, client entertainment, or remote workspace 
expense claims must be logged with valid receipts within the first week of the notice period. 
• 
PTO Payout Calculations: Any accrued, unused Paid Time Off (PTO) remaining in the 
employee's active balance will be calculated and paid out according to local labor 
regulations. 
4.3 The Exit Interview Framework 
Technova utilizes exit interviews as an open opportunity to gather candid feedback and continuously 
improve our internal operations. HR will coordinate a brief conversation during the employee's final 
two days of active service. This discussion focuses on gathering insights regarding workspace tools, 
technical infrastructure bottlenecks, team management dynamics, and overall growth opportunities. 
5.0 Post-Employment Conduct, Compliance, and FAQs 
5.1 Post-Separation Compliance Case Study: Handling IP Data 
• 
Scenario: An engineer completing their final week at Technova copies several custom scripts 
they authored onto a personal thumb drive to use as a personal reference at their next job. 
• 
Analysis: This action breaks our security and exit guidelines. All software code, technical 
briefs, and designs created during your employment belong exclusively to Technova and 
constitute sensitive proprietary IP. 
• 
Correct Action: The engineer must leave all data, code repos, and technical documentation 
completely within company systems. Extracting data onto personal storage media before an 
exit is flagged by automated system monitors and can lead to immediate legal review. 
5.2 Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 
Q1: Can I change my mind and rescind my resignation after logging it into the HRIS? A: Retracting a 
resignation notice is subject to executive leadership and department manager approval, depending 
on business requirements and whether a replacement has already been hired. 
Q2: How do I access my past pay stubs and tax documents after my corporate account is disabled? 
A: Following account deactivation, an alternate, personal login portal link will be transmitted to your 
verified personal email address, allowing secure access to past payroll records and tax forms. 
Q3: Who do I contact if my pre-paid hardware return container doesn't arrive on time? A: Reach 
out directly to the Central IT Logistics team via our external corporate helpdesk contact line to re-
verify your residential address coordinates and track your shipment.
